definition: No longer fashionable; out of date
example: Her clothes were new but passé.

definition: To describe or regard as worthy of disgrace or disapproval
example: She was stigmatised by society because her parents were unknown.

definition: Understood or implied without being stated
example: Management has given its tacit approval to the plan for renovation.

definition: A place where animals are slaughtered for food
example: Abattoirs are not places where kids should be taken.

definition: Extremely bad or hopeless; degrading
example: The beggars lived in abject poverty.

definition: A ritual or ceremonial washing of the body
example: Devotees perform their ablutions in the Ganges at dawn.

definition: An upward slope
example: The acclivity of the mountain made it impossible to climb.

definition: A willingness to take bold risks; rude boldness
example: He had the audacity to look at his watch while I was talking.

definition: To talk rapidly and in a foolish or unintelligible way
example: The old man is only babbling; don't pay attention.

definition: Shameless; undisguised
example: Barefaced lies about the project fooled no one.

definition: The use of trickery to achieve a political, financial or legal purpose
example: The trial revealed a world of crime, corruption and chicanery.

definition: A small, cramped space or compartment
example: Pigeons nest in cubbyholes on the sides of buildings.

definition: A downward slope
example: He slipped down the mountain because the declivity was too hard to manage.

definition: Worn out or broken down by age or hard use
example: The film was shot in a decrepit police station.

definition: A person who opposes official policy; (adjective) disagreeing, especially with a majority
example: Dissidents are found all too often in politics.

definition: Easily taught, managed or controlled
example: They were docile, obedient children.

definition: Asserting one's will over others in an arrogant way
example: His domineering nature made him difficult to work with.

definition: To impose an unwelcome or unwanted thing on someone
example: He foisted his work on me.

definition: A small mallet used by a presiding officer or judge to call for attention or order
example: The judge pounded his gavel to bring order to the proceedings.

definition: To confine within walls; to imprison
example: The con man was immured in prison for life.

definition: A situation in which no progress is possible
example: The government finds itself at an impasse over the Lokpal issue.

definition: Unable to be upset or excited; extremely calm
example: He was cool, aloof and imperturbable in all circumstances.

definition: Spotted or blotched
example: The maculate coat of the leopard helps it hide in foliage.

definition: To delay or postpone action needlessly
example: He procrastinated until it was almost too late to help anyone.

definition: A sharp, witty reply
example: His sharp retort made an impact.

definition: Unattractively thin and bony
example: She has a long, scrawny neck.

definition: To torment or tease with something desirable that is kept out of reach
example: He tantalised the dog with a piece of meat held just out of reach.

definition: To waver between different opinions or courses of action
example: She is vacillating over whether to marry him.
